text:
maria: quick heads-up — onboarding a HF chat model. model card includes a generation_config.json but our Redwood validation shows very low diversity and repeated token spans. anyone run into this when converting HF configs?

ben: can you paste the HF file? short snippet is fine. :eyes:

maria: here it is exactly from the repo:
```
{
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "top_p": 0.9,
  "top_k": 50,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.0,
  "do_sample": true,
  "eos_token_id": 50256
}
```
We converted it and the runtime got temperature=0.0 and outputs looked greedy.

kai: couple likely causes we see often: missing or false `do_sample` treated as deterministic, converter preferring `top_k` over `top_p` (kills nucleus), or subtle tokenization/template issues that double special token ids and skew repetition logic.

sam: repro from validation harness:``
[validate] model=hf-chat-x quant=4bit preset=rw-default
-> mapped params: temperature=0.0 top_k=50 top_p=null repetition_penalty=1.0
-> observed: repeated punctuation and special-token clusters
```
That temperature=0.0 is why it feels greedy.

eva: FYI we found one real bug earlier where templating concatenated sections with EOS twice, which produced consecutive identical token ids and made the repetition penalty appear to fire more often. snippet:``
template: <s> system ... </s> user ... </s> assistant ... </s>
token ids: ... 50256 50256 ...
```

ben: proposed a hardening checklist for HF->Redwood mapping:
- normalize numeric types and explicitly log fields present in HF metadata.
- deterministic case: if `do_sample` is false -> set temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0, top_k=1 and mark `deterministic=true` in conversion notes.
- sampling case: if `do_sample` missing/true -> honor `temperature`. if both `top_p` and `top_k` exist, prefer `top_p` (nucleus) but apply `top_k` as a hard cap after top-p filtering.
- repetition_penalty: treat <=1.0 as no-op; only apply >1.0. strip consecutive identical special tokens before applying penalty logic.
- ensure eos/pad/special token ids: if missing, derive from tokenizer.special_tokens_map and write the fallback to model metadata.
- persist every conversion decision into `model_metadata.conversion_notes` for audits.

kai: adding tests: matrix will include `do_sample=false`, `both top_k+top_p`, `repetition_penalty` edge cases, null/missing fields, and missing token ids. hooking tests into converter CI.

infra-bot: CI mapping-checks job started for branch/conv-fix -> https://ci.redwood.internal/4380 :white_check_mark:

ben: I'll implement the converter changes + a tiny regression that emits 10 short samples and asserts token repetition ratio < 0.07 and that runtime sampling config matches converted values (or deterministic override).

maria: also please add a one-paragraph blurb to the model onboarding checklist titled "HF generation_config gotchas" so new owners don't reintroduce this.

kai: will open a small docs PR and include the checklist and examples of offending HF payloads. assigning review to @ben.

maria: awesome — tagging the model owner in the ticket and leaving the HF file reference. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
